u.cycleNote: About 90 min on average. Adjust if you often wake before or after your alarm
u.heroBed: If you go to bed at {time}
u.napSub: {len}-min nap (alarm includes time to fall asleep)

u.warnPast: Bedtimes that allow {lo}+ hours have already passed. If you go to bed right now you can get up to about {d}. Getting to bed now matters more than matching cycles.

debt.title: Sleep debt log (last 7 days)
debt.note: Enter how long you actually slept each day to total the shortfall against your target. Saved in this browser only.
debt.warn: You are 5+ hours short this week. Going to bed 30-60 min earlier over several nights disrupts your rhythm less than one long weekend lie-in.
debt.tip: Extra sleep on some days is not subtracted from the shortfall (catch-up sleep does not fully repay it). General reference only.

sources: Recommended sleep by age: Hirshkowitz et al. (2015), National Sleep Foundation, Sleep Health 1(1):40-43
Adults: Watson et al. (2015), AASM/SRS consensus, J Clin Sleep Med 11(6):591 — 7+ hours per night for adults 18-60
Children/teens: Paruthi et al. (2016), AASM, J Clin Sleep Med 12(6):785 — 9-12h for ages 6-12, 8-10h for 13-18
Caffeine: Drake et al. (2013), J Clin Sleep Med 9(11):1195 — 400 mg caffeine even 6h before bed cut total sleep by over 1 hour
Naps: Brooks & Lack (2006), Sleep 29(6):831 — among 5/10/20/30-min naps, 10 min gave the strongest immediate benefit
Sleep cycles: about 90 min on average but 70-120 min, varying by person, night and cycle (Carskadon & Dement, Principles and Practice of Sleep Medicine)

sleepCalculator.title: Sleep Calculator
sleepCalculator.description: Find bedtimes for your wake-up time, when to wake if you sleep now, and nap alarms, based on sleep cycles
sleepCalculator.cycleExplanation: The 90-minute cycle is an average. Real cycles run roughly 70-120 minutes and vary by person and even between cycles in the same night, and time to fall asleep changes daily. Treat results as times you are more likely to wake less groggy; total sleep and a consistent wake time matter more than matching cycles.
sleepCalculator.ageGroupSource: Source: National Sleep Foundation (2015). The AASM recommends 7+ hours for adults, 9-12h for ages 6-12 and 8-10h for ages 13-18.
guideHabitsItems: Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day
Reduce screen time 1 hour before bed
Stop caffeine at least 6 hours before bed (by 5 PM for an 11 PM bedtime)
Keep your bedroom dark and cool (64-68°F / 18-20°C)
Exercise regularly but finish 3 hours before bedtime
guideScienceItems: 1 cycle = ~90 minutes (3 NREM stages N1–N3 + REM; about 70–120 min depending on the person and the cycle)
Waking from deep sleep (N3) leaves you groggy (sleep inertia); waking from REM makes dreams easier to recall
First 2 cycles (3 hours) have the most deep sleep
Adequate sleep is essential for memory, immunity, and mood
guideTipsItems: A warm shower before bed triggers cooling that induces sleep
Alcohol induces sleep but reduces sleep quality
Naps should be under 20 minutes, avoid after 3 PM
Use your bed only for sleep and relaxation
